system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Resubmitted with the verifier's two points repaired.

**Changes from the prior submission:**
1. **Customer convenience right now in operative language** — the old §4.1 wording sat inside the auto-renewal sentence, so it read as a non-renewal mechanic rather than an express mid-term Company exit. New §4.1A: "The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon ninety (90) days written notice to HDI specifying the Termination Date." Fallback element 1 is now addressed by operation, not claimed as already met.
2. **Cap anchored to the real compensation term** — the ceiling now reads "the amounts payable by the Company under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date," since HDI's compensation is the Net Sales percentage in §3.1 and the Agreement has no defined "fees" concept. This removes the argument that the cap is undefined or zero.

**Unchanged and deliberate:** the HDI term-end proviso in §4.1; HDI's 90-day notice remains already met by the retained mutual notice wording; the $800,000 deduction, the zero-floor in §4.2(b) and the quarterly instalments in §4.2(c) are untouched. We stay at the fallback rather than preferred (30 days / pro-rata refund) because payments run monthly in arrears on Net Sales, so there are no prepaid fees to refund. Minimality gate returned ok:true.

Rule and exact checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.",
  "Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.",
  "Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.",
  "Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.",
  "Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.",
  "Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.",
  "Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination."
]

Finding rationale:
Section 4.1 embeds the only exit mechanic in the auto-renewal sentence ("unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice"), and the notice merely "shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated". That gives HDI a self-dated mid-term walk-away while leaving the Company without an express convenience right, and any Company exit triggers an uncapped Termination Payment (half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales over $800,000). Those are three material fallback failures, so we target the fallback with the shortest edits: an express Company convenience right on ninety (90) days' notice, an HDI Termination Date fixed at the end of the then-current term, and a three-month cap on the Termination Payment measured by the amounts actually payable under Section 3.1 (the Net Sales-based compensation), so the ceiling is neither undefined nor arguably zero. HDI's 90-day notice obligation in the retained sentence already meets the fallback notice element for HDI; the favourable zero-floor in 4.2(b) and quarterly instalments in 4.2(c) still function under the cap.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

content.text: No transition or data-return provision exists anywhere; the termination section (4.1–4.2) addresses only notice and the Termination Payment. Let me validate an insert.

input.summary: Insert transition assistance and data return/deletion clause in Section 4
input.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement ends with no exit mechanics, so we have added a short Section 4.3: HDI provides up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, returns our Content and data in a standard machine-readable format within thirty days of expiry or termination, and certifies deletion after that return. If six months is too long, we can accept a 90-day assistance period with the same 30-day export.

ops.text: Transition Assistance; Return of Data. Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) provide the Company with transition assistance for up to six (6) months at HDI's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination, return to the Company all Content, user information and other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company in a standard machine-readable format; and (c) after such return, delete such Content, user information and data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to the Company.

reasons: Finding classification is correct: the original Section 9 contains only mutual corporate representations (organization, authority, enforceability, no conflicts) plus the Globix acknowledgement, and no performance, conformance or remedy warranty exists elsewhere in the cited text, so the clause fails every fallback element. There is no "AS IS" disclaimer, so this is a deviation (insert), not walk-away.

Fallback is complete on its face: 90-day documentation conformance for the Site and software, 30-day services conformance measured from performance, and repair/replace-or-refund remedies at HDI's option all appear in operative language rather than only in the margin comment.

Preferred remains unmet on five elements (professional and workmanlike standard, 12-month software period, 90-day services period, compliance with applicable laws, no malicious code). That is acceptable for a fallback-targeted redline, but note them in the rationale rather than treating them as additional deviations.

Repair recommendation (substance, not a completeness failure): the 90-day software/Site period runs "following the Effective Date" rather than following delivery or acceptance. In a site development and hosting agreement the Site is built after signature, so an Effective Date anchor risks the warranty expiring before or shortly after go-live. Change to "following delivery (or acceptance) of the Site" to track the model language and make the warranty operative.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",
  "Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination."
]

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

[

**Finding submitted: TRANSITION — missing (redline proposed).**

- **Investigated:** Section 4 (Term; Termination; Termination Payment — p0023–p0029), Section 8 (Confidentiality — no return-of-materials obligation), Section 10.7 (Survival — preserves only 6.3, 7, 9 and 10), and the hosting/export-file provisions in Sections 1.4–1.5. Searches for transition, data, return/export and machine-readable language returned no exit mechanics.
- **Conclusion:** HDI hosts the Site and holds our Content, user information and order data, yet the Agreement contains no transition assistance, no data return or export obligation, and no deletion terms — the rule's clause is genuinely absent.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule and exact checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):

Finding rationale:
Section 4 deals only with the term, notice of termination and the Termination Payment, and Section 10.7 (Survival) preserves Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 only. Nothing in the Agreement requires HDI, which hosts the Site and holds our Content, user information and order data, to provide any transition assistance, to return or export that data on expiry or termination, or to delete it afterwards. In a hosting agreement this absence is a deviation from the rule, so we insert a short Section 4.3 at the preferred level: up to six months' transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of our data in a standard machine-readable format within thirty days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion after that return. A 90-day assistance period with the same 30-day export is the acceptable fallback.

4.1 Term; Termination. This Agreement shall be effective as of that date (the "Effective Date") the Site becomes fully operational as set forth in writing and executed by both Parties and shall continue for a period of one (1) year from the Effective Date. This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other. (c) The Termination Payment, if any, shall be payable by the Company in eight (8) equal payments to be made quarterly, commencing thirty (30) days after the termination date.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) provide the Company with transition assistance for up to six (6) months at HDI's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination, return to the Company all Content, user information and other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company in a standard machine-readable format; and (c) after such return, delete such Content, user information and data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to the Company.
10.7 Survival. Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 of this Agreement shall survive and continue in full force and effect for a period of two years from the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon ninety (90) days written notice to HDI specifying the Termination Date." There are no Order Forms in this hosting agreement, so an Order-Form limb is unnecessary.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted Company right runs on "ninety (90) days written notice," which exceeds the 30-day preferred ceiling. To reach preferred the drafter would have to state 30 days or fewer.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language appears anywhere in the rendered text; Section 3.1 is a monthly Net Sales revenue share paid in arrears, but no operative pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts was added, so the element is unaddressed as drafted.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 as amended: "provided that a Termination Date specified by HDI shall be the end of the then-current term." The effective date of any HDI termination is expressly tied to term end, so HDI's exit is natural-term non-renewal rather than a mid-term convenience right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon ninety (90) days written notice to HDI specifying the Termination Date" — an express, unconditional Customer election at 90 days, inside the 60–90 day band.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) as amended: "provided that the Termination Payment shall not exceed the amounts payable by the Company under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date." The Termination Payment is the only early-exit charge, the cap basis is the Company's Section 3.1 compensation (a defined amount), and the measurement window is three months.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The Section 4.1 proviso fixes any HDI-specified Termination Date at "the end of the then-current term," expressly tying the effective date to term end rather than leaving HDI free to self-date a mid-term exit.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 4.1 language: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other" — HDI's notice obligation is 90 days and is unchanged by the edits.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: all four fallback elements are met in operative language (express 90-day Company convenience right; HDI Termination Date fixed at term end; Termination Payment capped at three months of Section 3.1 amounts; HDI's retained 90-day notice).

Preferred level fails on two elements — the Company notice period is 90 days rather than 30, and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees was added — but that is immaterial because the fallback checklist is fully satisfied.

Minimality holds: exactly three surgical edits, each traceable to a distinct unmet fallback element (Vendor term-end proviso, new Customer convenience sentence, cap proviso). No deletions, no survival tails, no added procedures, no 'in whole or in part' surplus (there are no Order Forms), and the favourable retained mechanics in 4.2(b)–(c) are untouched.

Intent preserved: the Termination Payment formula, the $800,000 deduction, the zero floor and quarterly instalments all continue to operate beneath the new ceiling; the cap basis references an existing defined section (3.1) so no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created, and the 'Termination Date' definition still functions for both parties.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Deerskin / HDI Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.2 — verified findings and redline positions

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. The dominant theme is omission rather than bad drafting: the Agreement is silent on indemnification, limitation of liability, insurance, IP ownership of the Site and deliverables, and post-termination transition and data return — all in a contract under which HDI designs, develops and hosts our Site and holds our Content, user information and order data. Section 9 ("Warranties") is limited to corporate authority representations and the Globix acknowledgement, and Section 10 (General Provisions) contains no ri[REDACTED] language at all.

Two findings are critical and both are absences: there is no HDI indemnity of any kind (including for third-party IP infringement), and there is no liability cap or consequential-damages exclusion, leaving both Parties with unlimited exposure. We propose inserting a Vendor indemnity at the preferred level and a single mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with standard uncapped carve-outs.

The high-severity items are the commercial restraints that run against us. Section 6.1 imposes an open-ended exclusivity and field-of-use restriction covering Deerskin Products "and products substantially similar", plus HDI's exclusive right over our own "Deerskin" brand online, with no duration cap because the term auto-renews annually under Section 4.1 and no performance-based exit. Section 4.2 requires the Company, on any termination, to pay HDI 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 in eight quarterly instalments — an uncapped stipulated sum far exceeding three months' fees — while Section 4.1 gives HDI a self-dated mid-term walk-away and leaves us without an express convenience right. Section 10.3 is a binding-effect provision only, so HDI is free to assign, including to a competitor.

Three provisions are compliant and require no redline: there is no MFN burdening us, no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment (fees are a pure revenue share above an $11,000 monthly threshold), and no non-solicitation covenant binding the Company. Section 10.5's choice of New York law also matches our preferred position; only venue is missing.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Missing | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a |
| 4 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and |
| 6 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a |
| 7 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and |
| 8 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a |
| 9 | Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and |
| 10 | Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and |
| 11 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and |
| 12 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a |
| 13 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and |
| 14 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and |
| 15 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a |
| 16 | Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and |
| 17 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a |
| 18 | Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and |

### Proposed positions on the open items

- **INDEMN (critical, missing).** Insert an HDI indemnity covering third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with standard notice, control and cooperation mechanics, plus a narrow reciprocal indemnity from us limited to Company-provided Content and our own breach of law. We deliberately do not add the fallback 3x-fees super-cap, which would introduce a new limit on HDI's exposure in an agreement that currently has no cap at all.
- **LOL-CAP (critical, missing).** Insert a single mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with a mutual indirect/consequential damages exclusion and uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP. Our payment obligations are expressly confirmed not to be damages subject to the cap. Placed as new Section 10.9, it survives under existing Section 10.7.
- **ASSIGN (high).** Add assignment mechanics after Section 10.3: our free assignment to affiliates and M&A successors; HDI assignment only with our consent, not unreasonably withheld, and never to a competitor; and express confirmation that our change of control gives HDI no termination right.
- **EXCLUSIVITY (high).** Redline Section 6.1 to the fallback: exclusivity confined to Deerskin Products, capped at twelve months from the Effective Date, terminating automatically on any HDI service-level or delivery-date failure. HDI's reciprocal covenant in Section 6.3 benefits us and is untouched.
- **LD (high).** Recast the Section 4.2 Termination Payment as an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees and declared the sole liquidated amount payable by us. We prefer this surgical edit to deletion, which would leave the retained machinery in 4.2(b)–(c) and the Section 4 heading dangling; 4.2(b) (no payment if the amount is zero or less) and 4.2(c) (instalments) remain coherent and favour us.
- **NONCOMPETE (high).** Convert Section 6.1 into an express permission, removing the restriction on "products substantially similar" and HDI's exclusive right over our own "Deerskin" brand. Section 6.3, which restricts HDI, is untouched. Noted but not flagged: the Section 9(b) proviso requiring termination of the Globix hosting agreement is a sourcing condition rather than a restriction on the businesses or products we may operate or build.
- **T4C (high).** Add an express Company convenience right on ninety days' notice; fix HDI's Termination Date at the end of the then-current term; and cap the Termination Payment at three months of the Section 3.1 amounts so the ceiling is neither undefined nor arguably zero.
- **GOVLAW (medium).** New York law in Section 10.5 already matches our preference; add one sentence conferring exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts in New York County, preserving only temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
- **LICENSE (medium).** Extend the Section 1.4 access/use grant to our affiliates on written notice. Successor transfer is already available through Section 10.3; contractor coverage and perpetual/irrevocable wording are preferred-level only and not pursued.
- **RENEWAL (medium).** Shorten the Section 4.1 non-renewal window from 90 to 60 days (the fallback ceiling). Renewal is on existing terms with no price-increase mechanic, so the price-cap element is not triggered; the absence of a vendor renewal reminder is a preferred-level refinement only.
- **TRANSITION (medium, missing).** Insert a new Section 4.3: up to six months' transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of our data in a standard machine-readable format within thirty days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion thereafter. Fallback: ninety days' assistance with the same thirty-day export.
- **WARRANTY (medium).** Insert the fallback warranty as new Section 9(c) — ninety days for the Site and software conforming to documentation, thirty days for the services — with repair, replacement or refund as our remedy. Placement preserves the Section 10.7 survival reference to Section 9.
- **AUDIT (low).** Section 3.4's notice, business-hours and cost provisions already meet or exceed the fallback; add a once-per-year cap on frequency. Independent-auditor and off-site refinements are not pursued as the clause is a records inspection only.
- **IP (low, missing).** Insert a new Section 5.5 granting us a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Site and other deliverables, with HDI retaining its generic tools and know-how and any HDI licence in our data limited to processing it solely to provide the services. Because HDI bears all development cost under Sections 1.2 and 1.6, we target this fallback rather than a full assignment.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the points our playbook treats as walk-away territory and where we should not sign as drafted:
